🇩🇿 Algerian rai music is one of Algeria's most iconic musical genres. It was born in the city of Oran, in western Algeria, during the early 20th century. Emerging from traditional Bedouin and folk songs performed by local singers, Raï gradually evolved by blending its rich heritage with modern instruments and rhythms. Its lyrics express everyday life, love, freedom, migration, and social issues, giving a voice to ordinary people. Thanks to the success of many Algerian artists, Raï music gained international recognition while proudly preserving its authentic Algerian identity and cultural roots. #algeria #rai #music #trending #fyp

On October 25, 2026, Algeria’s parliament unanimously approved sending army units to Niger, the first deployment of Algerian troops abroad since the 1973 war, when Algeria sent forces to support Egypt. The soldiers are expected to be stationed in Madama, in northern Niger near the Libyan border, at a former French military base. According to Algerian media, their mission could include protecting energy facilities and Sonatrach investments in the region. This comes after Algeria sent four Su-30 fighter jets to Niamey in August, following a failed mutiny. A major shift for an army that has stayed inside its borders for over 50 years. 🌍 #Algeria #algérie #Sahel #Africa #🇩🇿

In October 2026, a video from Algeria's Aïn Defla province went viral. Activist Hamid Fradj asked an orphaned bride what she needed for her wedding, and she answered, "Just two chickens," to feed her guests. Her simple request touched people across Algeria. Donations began arriving from different regions, including furniture, gold jewellery, groceries and help with food and decorations for the celebration. Reports say thousands of people gathered to celebrate with her on her wedding day. The bride is reportedly from the village of Sidi Lakhdar. Some details shared online, including long-term financial support, have not been verified. What would you do if you saw this video?
